decision: Bind mission-runtime benchmark evidence to a bounded host fingerprint
winner: Node/platform/arch + CPU model/logical CPU count + total memory, included in canonical evidence digest

reviews.correctness: Benchmark timings are not comparable from Git SHA and Node version alone; CPU and memory class materially affect rollback latency.
reviews.robustness_security: Fail closed on malformed host fingerprints and cover the fingerprint with the existing canonical SHA-256 evidence digest. This is integrity/comparability metadata, not trusted-origin authentication.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Reading os.cpus() and os.totalmem() is local and negligible, adds no worker/Qubes traffic, and avoids changing MissionQueue/Coordinator semantics while CI is unavailable.

alternatives_rejected.approach: Keep runtime fingerprint at Node/platform/arch only
alternatives_rejected.reason: Allows benchmark evidence from materially different host capacity to appear comparable.

alternatives_rejected.approach: Sign local evidence with a new private key
alternatives_rejected.reason: Adds key lifecycle and does not solve host comparability by itself; independent CI remains the release authority.
Raises correctness and regression surface without stable measurements proving exact snapshot rollback misses budgets.

qa: Schema v4 requires cpuModel, logicalCpus, and totalMemoryMiB.
Canonical evidence digest changes when host fingerprint changes.
Malformed or implausible host fingerprints fail closed.
Existing repeated-run budget and stability gates remain unchanged.
lessons: Performance evidence needs both code identity and execution-environment identity.
A SHA-256 evidence digest provides tamper detection, not source authentication.
Do not optimize rollback semantics until stable, comparable measurements justify it.
